taxonomic_note: Kew accepts Yucca constricta. FNA provides an especially useful field character: the dry capsule is deeply constricted near the middle.
look_here_first: Start with the narrow straight leaves and the fruit: Buckley’s yucca makes low colonies of small rosettes with narrow whitish-threaded leaves, an unusually tall naked scape, and dry capsules pinched deeply at the middle.
project_tracker_diagnostic: small to large open colonies, mostly acaulescent or with only a short stem; mostly straight linear leaves, usually about 0.7–1.5 cm wide; leaf margins whitish/light green and filiferous, shredding into threads; flowering stalk rises far above the leaves on a long naked scape; pale greenish-white pendent flowers; erect dry dehiscent capsule deeply constricted near the middle

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — UT Plant Resources Center Flora of Purola Preserve lists Yucca constricta among naturally occurring, non-introduced plants of northern Hays County. Travis — Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list for Travis County includes Buckley yucca (Yucca constricta). Val Verde — Laughlin Air Force Base Integrated Natural Resources Management Plan, Del Rio/Val Verde County, lists Yucca constricta among observed woody plants.

morphology_keys.joey_field_context: A Texas Observer field report documents Joey Santore pointing out Yucca constricta during a South Texas field visit. No exact reusable Joey species photo is locked yet, so the diagnostic morphology remains anchored to FNA/NPSOT rather than inferred from generic Yucca media.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Yucca rupicola: Y. constricta has narrow mostly straight white-threaded leaves and a deeply constricted capsule; Y. rupicola has broader flexible twisted leaves with orange/red denticulate margins. Yucca tenuistyla: Both have narrow filiferous leaves, but FNA separates Y. constricta by the deeply waist-constricted capsule; Y. tenuistyla capsules are not constricted and its leaves tend to recurve.
